# aibris v0.12.0

This feature/minor collects the work since v0.11.1: safer guided worktree
defaults, scan/cleanup accounting that matches what you can actually delete,
and install/release provenance. It is not a v0.11.2 patch.

## Highlights

- Guided cleanup no longer auto-selects worktrees whose HEAD is still unique
  versus local `origin/HEAD`. Those units stay reviewable. The probe is local
  Git only.
- Empty leftover worktree siblings and the registered `.orca-worktree-trash`
  sidecar no longer hide a valid owner as review-only `plain-dir`. Mixed
  invalid Git markers still fail closed.
- `scan` leads with found size, the largest reclaim path, and home-volume
  used%/free/band. Classic `clean --dry-run` lists targets largest-first.
- Go build-cache follows the live `$GOCACHE` / `go env -w` path. Explicit
  `--root` is a hard boundary and does not silently widen to extra Codex homes.
- Command cleanup reports observed `freed_bytes`. `clean --json` receipts add
  path-free `post_clean` volume and APFS remainder after mutation.
- Tagged releases publish SPDX SBOMs and GitHub attestations. The Homebrew
  tap updates only after the GitHub release is public.

## Compatibility impact

**Compatible addition**, plus safer guided default selection.

Documented CLI flags, defaults, and exit behavior are unchanged. Unique
worktrees that v0.11.x could auto-recommend now enter review as
`reviewable` instead of `recommended`; operators can still select them.
`schema_version` stays `1`. New optional `clean_receipt` field `post_clean`
and scan physical-total fields are additive. Consumers should ignore unknown
optional fields and stop on a newer unknown `schema_version`.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/sungjunlee/aibris/blob/v0.12.0/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete curated change list.

## Upgrade and migration

No flag migration is required.

```bash
brew upgrade aibris
# or:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sungjunlee/aibris/refs/heads/main/install.sh | bash -s -- 0.12.0
```

If a previous guided run auto-deleted unique-vs-`origin/HEAD` units and you
wanted that, those units are now reviewable: open guided review and select
them explicitly. They are not locked.

`scan --json` / `clean --json` consumers can ignore `post_clean` and
`physical_*` fields until they want them.

## Safety

- `plain-dir` and mixed-marker owners stay review-only and are never
  selected for deletion or strip.
- Empty leftover members and `.orca-worktree-trash` are not mixed markers;
  occupied unknown no-`.git` siblings still fail-close the owner.
- Unique-vs-default-branch content is not auto-recommended. GitHub is not
  contacted.
- Strip still refuses a unit that holds the current working directory.
- `--apfs-snapshots` stays opt-in and is never mixed into default clean.
- Default `clean --json` output stays path-redacted. Volume `id` is a hashed
  device token, not a mount path.

## Windows status

Windows archives are **experimental**. The supported shape is the `amd64` /
`arm64` Windows zip archives cross-built by GoReleaser and listed in
`checksums.txt`. Native users verify the SHA-256 and place `aibris.exe` on
`PATH`; `install.sh` remains Unix-only. Pull-request CI builds and exercises
the native executable (`--version`, `--help`, isolated `scan --json`), home /
cache isolation, recorded-cwd volume safety, reparse-point cleanup
protection, and hermetic HOME fixture behavior on `windows-latest`. A
Windows version matrix is not published.

## Verification

Pre-tag verification passed `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and the
Windows-status validator on this file. Focused `go test` covered worktree
classification, cleanup-unit agreement, and CLI contract fixtures. The tagged
release workflow publishes the six Darwin/Linux/Windows archives,
`checksums.txt`, SPDX SBOMs, GitHub attestations, and the tap Formula update.
